sanskrit: sa jitvā bhrātaraṃ rāma dhanadaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ mahāsenaprasūtiṃ tu yayau śaravaṇaṃ tataḥ
english: Having conquered his brother Kubera, O Rāma, the lord of rākṣasas proceeded thence to the Śaravaṇa forest, birthplace of great armies.

sanskrit: athāpaśyad daśagrīvo raukmaṃ śaravaṇaṃ tadā gabhastijālasaṃvītaṃ dvitīyam iva bhāskaram
english: Then Daśagrīva beheld that golden Śaravaṇa, wrapped in a network of rays, gleaming like a second sun.

sanskrit: parvataṃ sa samāsādya kiṃ cid ramyavanāntaram apaśyat puṣpakaṃ tatra rāma viṣṭambhitaṃ divi
english: Approaching the mountain, amid a charming grove, he saw there the Puṣpaka chariot, O Rāma, held motionless in the sky.

sanskrit: viṣṭabdhaṃ puṣpakaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmagaṃ hy agamaṃ kṛtam rākṣasaś cintayām āsa sacivais taiḥ samāvṛtaḥ
english: Seeing the Puṣpaka — that wish-propelled vehicle now rendered motionless — the rākṣasa reflected upon it, surrounded by his ministers.

sanskrit: kim idaṃ yannimittaṃ me na ca gacchati puṣpakam parvatasyoparisthasya kasya karma tv idaṃ bhavet
english: "What is this? Why does the Puṣpaka not move for me? Hovering above this mountain — whose deed can this be?"

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd daśagrīvaṃ mārīco buddhikovidaḥ naitan niṣkāraṇaṃ rājan puṣpako 'yaṃ na gacchati
english: Then Mārīca, wise in understanding, said to Daśagrīva: "It is not without cause, O king, that this Puṣpaka does not move."

sanskrit: tataḥ pārśvam upāgamya bhavasyānucaro balī nandīśvara uvācedaṃ rākṣasendram aśaṅkitaḥ
english: Then Nandiśvara, the mighty attendant of the Lord, drawing near to his side, fearlessly addressed the king of rākṣasas thus:

sanskrit: nivartasva daśagrīva śaile krīḍati śaṃkaraḥ
english: "Turn back, Daśagrīva — Śaṃkara is at sport upon this mountain."

sanskrit: suparṇanāgayakṣāṇāṃ daityadānavarakṣasām prāṇinām eva sarveṣām agamyaḥ parvataḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "This mountain has been made inaccessible to suparṇas, nāgas, yakṣas, daityas, dānavas, rākṣasas — to all living beings."

sanskrit: sa roṣāt tāmranayanaḥ puṣpakād avaruhya ca ko 'yaṃ śaṃkara ity uktvā śailamūlam upāgamat
english: He, his eyes reddened with anger, descended from the Puṣpaka and, saying "Who is this Śaṃkara?", strode to the base of the mountain.

sanskrit: nandīśvaram athāpaśyad avidūrasthitaṃ prabhum dīptaṃ śūlam avaṣṭabhya dvitīyam iva śaṃkaram
english: Then he beheld Nandiśvara standing not far away, his lord — gripping a blazing trident, like a second Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: sa vānaramukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tam avajñāya rākṣasaḥ prahāsaṃ mumuce maurkhyāt satoya iva toyadaḥ
english: The rākṣasa, seeing his monkey-face and despising him, broke into derisive laughter from sheer foolishness, like a rain-cloud releasing its waters.

sanskrit: saṃkruddho bhagavān nandī śaṃkarasyāparā tanuḥ abravīd rākṣasaṃ tatra daśagrīvam upasthitam
english: The blessed Nandī, wrathful — that other form of Śaṃkara himself — spoke to the rākṣasa Daśagrīva who stood before him:

sanskrit: yasmād vānaramūrtiṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasadurmate maurkhyāt tvam avajānīṣe parihāsaṃ ca muñcasi
english: "Because you, O wicked-minded rākṣasa, seeing me in the form of a monkey, have out of foolishness despised me and let loose your mockery —

sanskrit: tasmān madrūpasaṃyuktā madvīryasamatejasaḥ utpatsyante vadhārthaṃ hi kulasya tava vānarāḥ
english: "— therefore monkeys bearing my form, equal to me in might and energy, shall be born for the destruction of your lineage."

sanskrit: kiṃ tv idānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ kartuṃ yat tvāṃ niśācara na hantavyo hatas tvaṃ hi pūrvam eva svakarmabhiḥ
english: "Yet what can I do to you now, O night-wanderer? You are not to be slain by me — you are already slain, indeed, by your own deeds."

sanskrit: acintayitvā sa tadā nandivākyaṃ niśācaraḥ parvataṃ taṃ samāsādya vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Paying no heed to Nandī's words, the night-wanderer approached the mountain and spoke these words:

sanskrit: puṣpakasya gatiś chinnā yatkṛte mama gacchataḥ tad etac chailam unmūlaṃ karomi tava gopate
english: "For the sake of that which has cut off my Puṣpaka's flight as it traveled, I shall uproot this very mountain, O lord of cattle!"

sanskrit: kena prabhāvena bhavas tatra krīḍati rājavat vijñātavyaṃ na jānīṣe bhayasthānam upasthitam
english: "By what power does he sport there like a king? You should know — you do not know — that a danger stands before you."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rājan bhujān prakṣipya parvate tolayām āsa taṃ śailaṃ samṛgavyālapādapam
english: Having spoken thus, O king, he thrust his arms beneath the mountain and began to lift that peak, replete with deer, serpents, and trees.

sanskrit: tato rāma mahādevaḥ prahasan vīkṣya tatkṛtam pādāṅguṣṭhena taṃ śailaṃ pīḍayām āsa līlayā
english: Then, O Rāma, the great god Mahādeva, smiling and glancing at what had been done, pressed down upon that mountain with the tip of his toe — as if in play.

sanskrit: tatas te pīḍitās tasya śailasyādho gatā bhujāḥ vismitāś cābhavaṃs tatra sacivās tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: Then his arms, thrust beneath the mountain, were crushed, and his ministers who stood there were struck with astonishment.

sanskrit: rakṣasā tena roṣāc ca bhujānāṃ pīḍanāt tathā mukto virāvaḥ sumahāṃs trailokyaṃ yena pūritam
english: From the rākṣasa's anger and from the anguish of his crushed arms there burst forth an enormous roar by which the three worlds were filled.

sanskrit: mānuṣāḥ śabdavitrastā menire lokasaṃkṣayam devatāś cāpi saṃkṣubdhāś calitāḥ sveṣu karmasu
english: Human beings, terror-struck by the sound, believed it to be the dissolution of the world; the gods too were shaken and disturbed in their several duties.

sanskrit: tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ śailāgre viṣṭhitas tadā muktvā tasya bhujān rājan prāha vākyaṃ daśānanam
english: Then Mahādeva, pleased and standing on the summit of the mountain, released his arms, O king, and addressed Daśānana in these words:

sanskrit: prīto 'smi tava vīryāc ca śauṇḍīryāc ca niśācara ravato vedanā muktaḥ svaraḥ paramadāruṇaḥ
english: "I am pleased with your valor and your martial spirit, O night-wanderer; the cry released in your pain — that voice — was exceedingly terrible."

sanskrit: yasmāl lokatrayaṃ tv etad rāvitaṃ bhayam āgatam tasmāt tvaṃ rāvaṇo nāma nāmnā tena bhaviṣyasi
english: "Since all three worlds were made to resound and were seized with fear, therefore you shall henceforth be called Rāvaṇa by name."

sanskrit: devatā mānuṣā yakṣā ye cānye jagatītale evaṃ tvām abhidhāsyanti rāvaṇaṃ lokarāvaṇam
english: "Gods, humans, yakṣas, and all others who dwell on the earth's surface shall call you Rāvaṇa — he who makes the world cry out."

sanskrit: gaccha paulastya visrabdhaḥ pathā yena tvam icchasi mayā tvam abhyanujñāto rākṣasādhipa gamyatām
english: "Go, O son of Pulastya, at ease, by whatever path you wish — you are granted leave by me; depart, O lord of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: sākṣān maheśvareṇaivaṃ kṛtanāmā sa rāvaṇaḥ abhivādya mahādevaṃ vimānaṃ tat samāruhat
english: Thus named in person by Maheśvara, that Rāvaṇa paid homage to Mahādeva and mounted that celestial chariot.

sanskrit: tato mahītale rāma paricakrāma rāvaṇaḥ kṣatriyān sumahāvīryān bādhamānas tatas tataḥ
english: Thereafter, O Rāma, Rāvaṇa roamed across the earth, harassing mighty kṣatriyas here and there.

sanskrit: atha rājan mahābāhur vicaran sa mahītalam himavadvanam āsādya paricakrāma rāvaṇaḥ
english: Then, O king, the long-armed one, wandering over the earth, reached the Himālayan forest and roamed through it — Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyata vai kanyāṃ kṛṣṭājinajaṭādharām ārṣeṇa vidhinā yuktāṃ tapantīṃ devatām iva
english: There he saw a maiden clad in a rough antelope-skin and matted locks, engaged in austerity according to the sage's prescribed rite, like a goddess performing her penance.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā rūpasaṃpannāṃ kanyāṃ tāṃ sumahāvratām kāmamohaparītātmā papraccha prahasann iva
english: Seeing that maiden endowed with beauty and of exceedingly great vows, his mind overpowered by the intoxication of desire, he questioned her as if with a smile:

sanskrit: kim idaṃ vartase bhadre viruddhaṃ yauvanasya te na hi yuktā tavaitasya rūpasyeyaṃ pratikriyā
english: "Why do you practice this, O fortunate one, which is contrary to your youth? This mode of conduct is not fitting for one of your beauty."

sanskrit: kasyāsi duhitā bhadre ko vā bhartā tavānaghe pṛcchataḥ śaṃsa me śīghraṃ ko vā hetus tapo'rjane
english: "Whose daughter are you, O fortunate one? Who is your husband, O sinless one? Tell me quickly, as I ask — what is the reason for your pursuit of austerity?"

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā kanyā tenānāryeṇa rakṣasā abravīd vidhivat kṛtvā tasyātithyaṃ tapodhanā
english: Thus addressed by that ignoble rākṣasa, the maiden, rich in ascetic power, offered him guest-honor according to the proper rite and spoke:

sanskrit: kuśadhvajo nāma pitā brahmarṣir mama dhārmikaḥ bṛhaspatisutaḥ śrīmān buddhyā tulyo bṛhaspateḥ
english: "My father was named Kuśadhvaja, a brahmarṣi, righteous, the son of Bṛhaspati, glorious, equal to Bṛhaspati in wisdom."

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ kurvato nityaṃ vedābhyāsaṃ mahātmanaḥ saṃbhūtā vānmayī kanyā nāmnā vedavatī smṛtā
english: "I was born of that great soul as he constantly practiced study of the Vedas — born as a maiden made of speech itself, known by the name Vedavatī."

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ te cāpi gatvā pitaraṃ varaṇaṃ rocayanti me
english: "Then gods together with gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and serpents — they too went to my father and proposed me as their bride."

sanskrit: na ca māṃ sa pitā tebhyo dattavān rākṣaseśvara kāraṇaṃ tad vadiṣyāmi niśāmaya mahābhuja
english: "But my father did not give me to any of them, O lord of rākṣasas. I shall tell you the reason — hear it, O great-armed one."

sanskrit: pitus tu mama jāmātā viṣṇuḥ kila surottamaḥ abhipretas trilokeśas tasmān nānyasya me pitāḥ
english: "My father's intended son-in-law was Viṣṇu himself, the best of gods, the lord of the three worlds — to none other would my father give me."

sanskrit: dātum icchati dharmātmā tac chrutvā baladarpitaḥ śambhur nāma tato rājā daityānāṃ kupito 'bhavat tena rātrau prasupto me pitā pāpena hiṃsitaḥ
english: "Learning that the righteous-souled one wished to give me thus, a daitya king named Śambhu, arrogant with power, grew enraged — and that wicked one slew my sleeping father in the night."

sanskrit: tato me jananī dīnā tac charīraṃ pitur mama pariṣvajya mahābhāgā praviṣṭā dahanaṃ saha
english: "Then my mother, wretched, embracing my father's body, that most noble one entered the fire along with him."

sanskrit: tato manorathaṃ satyaṃ pitur nārāyaṇaṃ prati karomīti mamecchā ca hṛdaye sādhu viṣṭhitā
english: "Then the wish to fulfill my father's true longing regarding Nārāyaṇa settled firmly in my heart: 'I shall accomplish it.'"

sanskrit: ahaṃ pretagatasyāpi kariṣye kāṅkṣitaṃ pituḥ iti pratijñām āruhya carāmi vipulaṃ tapaḥ
english: "Even for my father who has gone to the realm of the dead I will fulfill his desire — having taken this vow, I practice extensive austerity."

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ mayā rākṣasapuṃgava āśritāṃ viddhi māṃ dharmaṃ nārāyaṇapatīcchayā
english: "All this has been told to you by me, O foremost of rākṣasas. Know me to be one who has taken refuge in dharma, with the desire to have Nārāyaṇa as my lord."

sanskrit: vijñātas tvaṃ hi me rājan gaccha paulastyanandana jānāmi tapasā sarvaṃ trailokye yad dhi vartate
english: "I know who you are, O king. Go, O son of Paulastya's lineage. Through my austerity I know all that transpires in the three worlds."

sanskrit: so 'bravīd rāvaṇas tatra tāṃ kanyāṃ sumahāvratām avaruhya vimānāgrāt kandarpaśarapīḍitaḥ
english: Then Rāvaṇa, wounded by the arrows of Kandarpа, descended from the prow of his chariot and addressed that maiden of exceedingly great vows:

sanskrit: avaliptāsi suśroṇi yasyās te matir īdṛśī vṛddhānāṃ mṛgaśāvākṣi bhrājate dharmasaṃcayaḥ
english: "You are conceited, O lovely-hipped one, whose mind runs in such a direction — it is old people, O doe-eyed maiden, in whom the accumulation of dharma shines."

sanskrit: tvaṃ sarvaguṇasaṃpannā nārhase kartum īdṛśam trailokyasundarī bhīru yauvane vārdhakaṃ vidhim
english: "You are endowed with every virtue and do not deserve to do this. You are the most beautiful in all three worlds, O timid one — to follow the ways of old age in youth!"

sanskrit: kaś ca tāvad asau yaṃ tvaṃ viṣṇur ity abhibhāṣase vīryeṇa tapasā caiva bhogena ca balena ca na mayāsau samo bhadre yaṃ tvaṃ kāmayase 'ṅgane
english: "And who then is that one whom you speak of as Viṣṇu? In valor, in austerity, in enjoyment, and in strength, he is not my equal, O fortunate one — he whom you desire, O slender-waisted maiden."

sanskrit: ma maivam iti sā kanyā tam uvāca niśācaram mūrdhajeṣu ca tāṃ rakṣaḥ karāgreṇa parāmṛśat
english: "No, do not — do not speak thus!" — so the maiden said to that night-wanderer. But the rākṣasa touched her hair with the tip of his hand.

sanskrit: tato vedavatī kruddhā keśān hastena sācchinat uvācāgniṃ samādhāya maraṇāya kṛtatvarā
english: Then Vedavatī, enraged, cut off her own hair with her hand, kindled a fire, and, resolved upon death, spoke:

sanskrit: dharṣitāyās tvayānārya nedānīṃ mama jīvitam rakṣas tasmāt pravekṣyāmi paśyatas te hutāśanam
english: "Violated by you, O ignoble one, life is no longer mine, O rākṣasa. Therefore I shall enter the fire as you watch."

sanskrit: yasmāt tu dharṣitā cāham apāpā cāpy anāthavat tasmāt tava vadhārthaṃ vai samutpatsyāmy ahaṃ punaḥ
english: "And since I, though without sin, have been violated as if unprotected, therefore I shall be born again for the sake of your destruction."

sanskrit: na hi śakyaḥ striyā pāpa hantuṃ tvaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ śāpe tvayi mayotsṛṣṭe tapasaś ca vyayo bhavet
english: "For you, O wicked one, cannot be slain by a woman — certainly not by me. And if a curse were cast on you, my austerity would be diminished."

sanskrit: yadi tv asti mayā kiṃ cit kṛtaṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ tathā tena hy ayonijā sādhvī bhaveyaṃ dharmiṇaḥ sutā
english: "But if there is any deed done, gift given, or oblation offered by me, by that merit may I — virtuous one, not born of a womb — become the daughter of a righteous man."

sanskrit: evam uktvā praviṣṭā sā jvalantaṃ vai hutāśanam papāta ca divo divyā puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ
english: Having spoken thus, she entered the blazing fire; and from the sky a divine rain of flowers fell all around.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ krodhahataḥ śatrur yayāsau nihatas tvayā samupāśritya śailābhaṃ tava vīryam amānuṣam
english: "The enemy struck down by your wrath of old — he who was slain by you when he had taken refuge relying on your mountain-like, superhuman valor —"

sanskrit: evam eṣā mahābhāgā martyeṣūtpadyate punaḥ kṣetre halamukhagraste vedyām agniśikhopamā
english: "— thus this most blessed one is born again among mortals, drawn forth by a plowshare's tip from the field, upon the sacrificial altar, like a flame of fire."

sanskrit: eṣā vedavatī nāma pūrvam āsīt kṛte yuge tretāyugam anuprāpya vadhārthaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ sītotpanneti sītaiṣā mānuṣaiḥ punar ucyate
english: "This one who was formerly named Vedavatī in the Kṛta age — having reached the Tretā age, born for the slaying of that rākṣasa, she arose as Sītā; she is this Sītā, called again by humans."

sanskrit: praviṣṭāyāṃ hutāśaṃ tu vedavatyāṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ puṣpakaṃ tat samāruhya paricakrāma medinīm
english: When Vedavatī had entered the fire, Rāvaṇa mounted that Puṣpaka chariot and continued to roam the earth.

sanskrit: tato maruttaṃ nṛpatiṃ yajantaṃ saha daivataiḥ uśīrabījam āsādya dadarśa sa tu rākṣasaḥ
english: Then, reaching Uśīrabīja, that rākṣasa saw king Marutta performing a sacrifice together with the gods.

sanskrit: saṃvarto nāma brahmarṣir bhrātā sākṣād bṛhaspateḥ yājayām āsa dharmajñaḥ sarvair brahmagaṇair vṛtaḥ
english: A brahmarṣi named Saṃvarta, the very brother of Bṛhaspati, versed in dharma, was officiating at the sacrifice, surrounded by all the hosts of brahmin priests.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā devās tu tad rakṣo varadānena durjayam tāṃ tāṃ yoniṃ samāpannās tasya dharṣaṇabhīravaḥ
english: The gods, seeing that rākṣasa who was unconquerable by reason of boons received, assumed various animal forms, fearful of being harassed by him.

sanskrit: indro mayūraḥ saṃvṛtto dharmarājas tu vāyasaḥ kṛkalāso dhanādhyakṣo haṃso vai varuṇo 'bhavat
english: Indra became a peacock; the king of dharma became a crow; the lord of wealth became a lizard; Varuṇa indeed became a swan.

sanskrit: taṃ ca rājānam āsādya rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ prāha yuddhaṃ prayacceti nirjito 'smīti vā vada
english: Approaching that king, Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, said: "Give me battle — or else say 'I am defeated.'"

sanskrit: tato marutto nṛpatiḥ ko bhavān ity uvāca tam avahāsaṃ tato muktvā rākṣaso vākyam abravīt
english: Then king Marutta said to him "Who are you?" — whereupon the rākṣasa, letting out a laugh of contempt, spoke these words:

sanskrit: akutūhalabhāvena prīto 'smi tava pārthiva dhanadasyānujaṃ yo māṃ nāvagacchasi rāvaṇam
english: "I am pleased by your nonchalant manner, O king — you who do not recognize me as Rāvaṇa, the younger brother of Kubera."

sanskrit: triṣu lokeṣu kaḥ so 'sti yo na jānāti me balam bhrātaraṃ yena nirjitya vimānam idam āhṛtam
english: "Who is there in the three worlds that does not know my might — I who, having conquered my own brother, seized this chariot?"

sanskrit: tato marutto nṛpatis taṃ rākṣasam athābravīt dhanyaḥ khalu bhavān yena jyeṣṭho bhrātā raṇe jitaḥ
english: Then king Marutta addressed that rākṣasa: "Fortunate indeed are you, by whom your elder brother was conquered in battle!"

sanskrit: nādharmasahitaṃ ślāghyaṃ na lokapratisaṃhitam karma daurātmyakaṃ kṛtvā ślāghase bhrātṛnirjayāt
english: "What is accompanied by adharma is not praiseworthy; what is contrary to the world's good is not praiseworthy. Having done a deed of wickedness, you boast of having defeated your own brother."

sanskrit: kiṃ tvaṃ prāk kevalaṃ dharmaṃ caritvā labdhavān varam śrutapūrvaṃ hi na mayā yādṛśaṃ bhāṣase svayam
english: "Did you first practice dharma alone and then obtain the boon? For I have not heard before of the kind of thing you now proclaim yourself."

sanskrit: tataḥ śarāsanaṃ gṛhya sāyakāṃś ca sa pārthivaḥ raṇāya niryayau kruddhaḥ saṃvarto mārgam āvṛṇot
english: Then that king, seizing his bow and arrows, set forth furiously for battle — but Saṃvarta blocked his path.

sanskrit: so 'bravīt snehasaṃyuktaṃ maruttaṃ taṃ mahān ṛṣiḥ śrotavyaṃ yadi madvākyaṃ saṃprahāro na te kṣamaḥ
english: The great ṛṣi spoke to Marutta with affection: "If my word is to be heeded, engagement in combat is not appropriate for you."

sanskrit: māheśvaram idaṃ satram asamāptaṃ kulaṃ dahet dīkṣitasya kuto yuddhaṃ krūratvaṃ dīkṣite kutaḥ
english: "This sacrifice to Maheśvara, if left incomplete, would burn up your lineage. How can one who is consecrated engage in war? How can there be cruelty in one who is consecrated?"

sanskrit: saṃśayaś ca raṇe nityaṃ rākṣasaś caiṣa durjayaḥ sa nivṛtto guror vākyān maruttaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ svastho makhamukho 'bhavat
english: "And in battle there is always uncertainty, and this rākṣasa is hard to conquer." Thereupon king Marutta, lord of the earth, turned back at his guru's word, laid aside his arrow-strung bow, composed himself, and faced the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ nirjitaṃ matvā ghoṣayām āsa vai śukaḥ rāvaṇo jitavāṃś ceti harṣān nādaṃ ca muktavān
english: Then Śuka, considering him defeated, proclaimed it aloud — "Rāvaṇa has won!" — and out of joy let loose a shout.

sanskrit: tān bhakṣayitvā tatrasthān maharṣīn yajñam āgatān vitṛpto rudhirais teṣāṃ punaḥ saṃprayayau mahīm
english: Having devoured the great ṛṣis who were present there, gathered for the sacrifice, and satiated with their blood, he set forth again across the earth.

sanskrit: rāvaṇe tu gate devāḥ sendrāś caiva divaukasaḥ tataḥ svāṃ yonim āsādya tāni sattvāny athābruvan
english: When Rāvaṇa had departed, the gods, together with Indra, the dwellers in heaven, resumed their own forms; and then they addressed those creatures thus:

sanskrit: harṣāt tadābravīd indro mayūraṃ nīlabarhiṇam prīto 'smi tava dharmajña upakārād vihaṃgama
english: Then Indra, out of joy, addressed the peacock with blue plumage: "I am pleased with you for your service, O wise-in-dharma, O bird."

sanskrit: mama netrasahasraṃ yat tat te barhe bhaviṣyati varṣamāṇe mayi mudaṃ prāpsyase prītilakṣaṇam
english: "The thousand eyes that are mine — those shall appear upon your tail-feathers; and when I rain, you shall experience delight — this is the mark of my favor."

sanskrit: nīlāḥ kila purā barhā mayūrāṇāṃ narādhipa surādhipād varaṃ prāpya gatāḥ sarve vicitratām
english: "The tail-feathers of peacocks were formerly all blue, O lord of men; having received the boon from the lord of gods, they all took on their variegated splendor."

sanskrit: dharmarājo 'bravīd rāma prāgvaṃśe vāyasaṃ sthitam pakṣiṃs tavāsmi suprītaḥ prītasya ca vacaḥ śṛṇu
english: The king of dharma, O Rāma, addressed the crow perched in the eastern hall: "O bird, I am most pleased with you; hear the word of one who is pleased."

sanskrit: yathānye vividhai rogaiḥ pīḍyante prāṇino mayā te na te prabhaviṣyanti mayi prīte na saṃśayaḥ
english: "The various diseases by which other living beings are afflicted at my hand — those shall have no power over you, now that I am pleased — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: mṛtyutas te bhayaṃ nāsti varān mama vihaṃgama yāvat tvāṃ na vadhiṣyanti narās tāvad bhaviṣyasi
english: "You have no fear of death from my boons, O bird — until men slay you, you shall endure."

sanskrit: ye ca madviṣayasthās tu mānavāḥ kṣudhayārditāḥ tvayi bhukte tu tṛptās te bhaviṣyanti sabāndhavāḥ
english: "And those humans dwelling in my domain who are tormented by hunger — when you have eaten, they too shall be satisfied along with their kinsmen."

sanskrit: varuṇas tv abravīd dhaṃsaṃ gaṅgātoyavicāriṇam śrūyatāṃ prītisaṃyuktaṃ vacaḥ patraratheśvara
english: Varuṇa then addressed the swan that moves upon the waters of the Gaṅgā: "Hear these words spoken with affection, O lord among winged ones."

sanskrit: varṇo manoharaḥ saumyaś candramaṇḍalasaṃnibhaḥ bhaviṣyati tavodagraḥ śuklaphenasamaprabhaḥ
english: "A color enchanting and beautiful, resembling the disk of the moon — it shall arise in you, lofty and gleaming like white foam."

sanskrit: maccharīraṃ samāsādya kānto nityaṃ bhaviṣyasi prāpsyase cātulāṃ prītim etan me prītilakṣaṇam
english: "Having attained likeness to my body, you shall always be beautiful, and you shall obtain incomparable delight — this is the mark of my favor."

sanskrit: haṃsānāṃ hi purā rāma na varṇaḥ sarvapāṇḍuraḥ pakṣā nīlāgrasaṃvītāḥ kroḍāḥ śaṣpāgranirmalāḥ
english: "For formerly, O Rāma, the color of swans was not entirely white — their wings were tipped with blue at the ends, their breasts were pure as fresh grass-tips."

sanskrit: athābravīd vaiśravaṇaḥ kṛkalāsaṃ girau sthitam hairaṇyaṃ saṃprayacchāmi varṇaṃ prītis tavāpy aham
english: Then Vaiśravaṇa addressed the lizard standing on the mountain: "I bestow upon you a golden color — this too is my affection for you."

sanskrit: sadravyaṃ ca śiro nityaṃ bhaviṣyati tavākṣayam eṣa kāñcanako varṇo matprītyā te bhaviṣyati
english: "Your head shall always bear wealth upon it, imperishable; this golden hue shall be yours by my favor."

sanskrit: evaṃ dattvā varāṃs tebhyas tasmin yajñotsave surāḥ nivṛtte saha rājñā vai punaḥ svabhavanaṃ gatāḥ
english: Having thus bestowed boons upon them at that sacrificial festival, the gods, when it was concluded together with the king, returned each to their own abode.
